comparison: Both strongly support the validation of gene editing and functional heterotrimers (C31-C37). OpenEval emphasizes converging evidence from multiple assays, while peer reviewers praised technical rigor and careful execution. High agreement on methodological quality.

Both address G protein heterotrimer assembly and stoichiometry (C38-C41). OpenEval finds claims well-supported by literature, while peer reviewers express uncertainty, noting the reasoning is convincing but experimental demonstration of G-beta assembly status is lacking. Key disagreement on evidence sufficiency.

Both support plasma membrane and organelle localization findings. OpenEval focuses on C42-C46, C8 (plasma membrane, lysosomes, absence from ER/mitochondria/Golgi), while peer R2 covers broader localization claims including endosomes (C6, C7, C24, C42-C47, C51-C53, C55, C57). Strong agreement on localization patterns.

OpenEval R4 addresses endosome colocalization and quantification (C47-C54, C6, C24), overlapping with peer R2's broader localization assessment. Both support the finding of G proteins on endosomes with lower intensity than plasma membrane. Agreement on endosomal presence.

Partial overlap on quantitative endosome findings (C48, C49, C54). Both support low abundance on early endosomes. Peer R4 includes additional quantification claims (C5, C25, C26, C61, C64-C66) about partial exclusion from endocytic vesicles. Agreement on quantitative measurements.

OpenEval R5 focuses on lysosomal localization (C55-C56, C7), which is part of peer R2's broader localization assessment. Both support strong lysosomal G protein presence with intensity similar to plasma membrane. Agreement on lysosomal findings.

OpenEval R6 addresses trans-Golgi network localization (C57), which is included in peer R2's comprehensive localization evaluation. Both support presence on trans-Golgi network despite absence from medial-trans Golgi. Agreement on Golgi subcompartment distribution.

Perfect match on bystander BRET validation (C60). Both strongly support this orthogonal method for confirming imaging results. Peer reviewers explicitly praised the convergence of two independent methods (microscopy and BRET) as inspiring confidence. Strong agreement on methodological validation.

Both address partial exclusion of G proteins from endocytic vesicles using FM4-64 comparison (C5, C25, C26, C62-C66). OpenEval emphasizes sound methodology and appropriate quantification, peer reviewers accepted findings without challenge. Strong agreement on quantitative exclusion measurements.

Perfect match on mNG-HRas control experiment (C67). Both support this validation showing differential exclusion of peripheral membrane proteins. Neither evaluation questioned this control, viewing it as strengthening the main findings. Complete agreement.

Both address receptor activation effects on G protein distribution (C27, C68-C71). OpenEval also includes C73-C74 on BRET changes. Both strongly support the conclusion that receptor activation does not regulate G protein endocytosis. Peer reviewers affirmed no shuttling with activated receptors. Strong agreement.

OpenEval R11 focuses on BRET data during activation (C72-C74, C9), overlapping with peer R5's assessment of activation effects. Both support reversible changes during activation but no lasting distribution changes. Agreement on transient activation-dependent effects.

Both address transient BRET changes during activation (C72). OpenEval provides detailed analysis of reversible changes, peer reviewers accepted this as consistent with known translocation patterns. Agreement on transient activation effects.

Both address trafficking inferences and functional implications (C58-C59, C91-C92, C94-C95). OpenEval notes these are reasonable inferences rather than direct demonstrations. Peer R6 also includes broader functional implications (C10, C28, C76, C88). Both accept these as reasonable interpretations with significant implications for GPCR signaling. Agreement on inferred trafficking dynamics.

Partial overlap on functional implications of inefficient endocytosis (C28, C76, C88). OpenEval R13 also includes C75, C109 on collision-limited coupling. Both support these functional inferences as reasonable conclusions from the data. Agreement on functional significance.

Both address the overarching conclusion about G protein localization preferences (C83, C106). OpenEval emphasizes absence from ER despite being formation site, peer reviewers strongly endorsed the main finding of preference for plasma and lysosomal membranes. Strong agreement on central conclusion.

Perfect match on bystander BRET methodological contribution (C97-C98). Both support this as a valuable approach. Peer reviewers explicitly praised the elegant extension of gene editing strategy combined with FRET-based proximity assay. Strong agreement on methodological innovation.

Perfect match on study limitations (C99-C102, C104-C105). Both appropriately acknowledge caveats without viewing them as invalidating findings. Peer reviewers noted these as directions for future work rather than fatal flaws. Complete agreement on appropriate qualification of conclusions.

OpenEval evaluates size-dependent steric occlusion mechanism (C78-C80) as uncertain/speculative. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though this speculation appears in the manuscript discussion.
OpenEval notes independent validation by Hein et al., 2023 proteomics study (C89). No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing this external validation.

OpenEval evaluates potential exceptions involving specific G protein types or cell contexts (C93, C103) as uncertain/speculative. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific caveats.
